//: Virtual models for both Pi profiles, read by ~/.pi/shared/extensions/profile. Each is listed under its profile's provider id (personal/daily, work/fast, ...). On a new prompt the router takes the first target that is usable and inside its usage budget; tool loops and compaction stay on the model that answered last. A failure falls back down the chain within the same billing class. Reasoning behind every choice: ~/.pi/shared/README.md.
//providers: billing: what a request spends. usage: the subscription pool it draws on (tracked in <agent-dir>/usage.json by usage-sources.ts). failsOverInternally: the provider already retried and failed over (LiteLLM), so a failure there skips its other targets.
//usage: Pools are re-read every refreshMinutes and ignored once older than staleMinutes (unknown = no preference). At exhaustedPercent, or when the plan reports its limit, a pool is skipped outright. Otherwise a target is skipped on a new prompt when its pool is at or over maxUsed (default defaultMaxUsed), or, with paced, when a window is more than paceSlack points ahead of its elapsed time. If every target is over budget the first usable one still runs; budgets steer, they never block. Above stickyAboveTokens (estimated conversation size) a new prompt stays on the model that answered last unless a hard limit forces a move (exhausted, no login, images, provider policy) or a failure fallback for another target is active: every provider's prompt cache is per model, so a budget-driven switch mid-conversation costs more than it saves.
//tuning: transientRetriesPerModel: retries of the same target after an overloaded/5xx/network error before moving down the chain. stickyFallbackMinutes: how long later prompts stay on a failure fallback before trying the primary again.

daily.name: Daily
daily.//: Opus while the Claude week is on pace, then Sonnet (≈ Opus on TB4 at about half the plan usage), then GPT-6.1 Sol, GLM-5.3 (best open model; text only) and MiniMax M3 (images) as the pools fill.

deep.name: Deep
deep.//: Strongest available at high effort: Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol (≈ 90% of Astra on TB4 at a fifth of the Codex credits), GLM-5.3, then Qwen3.8 Max for prompts with images.

fast.name: Fast
fast.//: MiniMax M3 first (near-unlimited plan, images), then DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (fastest; spends the shared Go pool), then GPT-6 Luna (≈1% of Sol's Codex credits).

local.name: Local (BC250)
local.//: LiteLLM's local-only alias: no gateway fallbacks and none here either, not even on context overflow (Pi compacts instead).
local.unavailableHint: The BC250 may be offline; use personal/qwen (LiteLLM falls back to MiniMax M3) or another model.

qwen.name: Qwen (BC250, MiniMax M3 when off)
qwen.//: LiteLLM's bc250 alias: the local Qwen while the BC250 is up, MiniMax M3 (through the gateway) while it is not. Pi adds no fallback of its own.

personal.//auto: personal/auto (the startup default): MiniMax M3 reads each new prompt and picks fast, daily or deep; that tier's chain then picks the model by usage. Short follow-ups skip the call, a long conversation is not moved down a tier (prompt cache), and a slow or failed classifier keeps the current tier.

work.//: Enterprise Claude seat only, through pi-claude-bridge logged into ~/.pi/profiles/work/agent/claude. The seat is spend-metered with a small monthly allowance, so Sonnet does daily work and Opus is kept for deep work; budgets step down as the month's spend grows.

//advisors: On-demand second opinions through the `advisor` tool; never selectable as chat models. Each consultation runs as a separate pi process with read-only tools and memory capture off. With no advisor named, the first in `order` whose pool is not exhausted or over 90% is used.
